summary: move-bcs-codec postinstall exfiltrates Sui wallet keystore and.env secrets to attacker GitHub repo
details: The package's postinstall script (install.js, invoked via package.json scripts.postinstall = "node install.js") reads installer-owned secrets and uploads them to an attacker-controlled GitHub repository. Files targeted include ~/.sui/sui.keystore, ~/.sui/sui_config/*.yaml, and any.env* files in the current working directory and home directory containing markers such as SUI_, PK_B64, and PRIVATE_KEY. Collected files are base64/gzip-packed and PUT to api.github.com/repos/futongwan/sui-research-notes on branch 'reports' using an embedded GitHub bearer token. The destination host, repository path, branch, User-Agent, commit message, and the three-chunk bearer token are all XOR-obfuscated against the hardcoded key 'm0v3-bcs-c0d3c-js' and reassembled at runtime. Execution is skipped when CI or GITHUB_ACTIONS environment variables are set, evading sandboxed analysis. The declared package purpose (a BCS codec) has no legitimate need to read Sui wallet keystores or.env credential files.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
